Rashi on Chullin 51a:10:2.english: That they are in pain - [They are] distressed and in pain.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:10:3.hebrew: צימרא - חמימות, כמו (שבת דף סז.) אישתא צמירתא:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:10:3.english: A fever - Heat, as in (Shabbat 67a): “A burning fever.”

Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:1.hebrew: דגנבי גנבי - ומשליכין אותם למעלה מכתלי החצר, ונופלים לארץ:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:1.english: That thieves steal - And [the thieves] throw them over the walls of the courtyard, and they fall to the ground.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:2.hebrew: אמתנייהו - על מתניהן נופלין, ואין נהפכין על גבן שיתפרקו חוליותיהן:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:2.english: On their hips - They land on their hips and do not overturn onto their backs, so that their vertebrae would become dislocated.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:3.english: [If] they returned them - By way of [throwing them] over the wall.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:11:4.english: We certainly must be concerned - For they do not care however it falls.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:1.english: [If] one hit on its head - That he tilted the staff.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:2.hebrew: והלכה לה כלפי זנבה - והכה על מתניה, ולא על הצלעות; וכן על זנבה והלכה כלפי ראשה — והכה על צוארה. "ואפילו" — ל"ג, דדוקא לא כפף המטה והכה על כל הצלעות — "כנגד כל השדרה" קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:2.english: And it went toward its tail - And struck upon its loins, and not upon the ribs; and likewise, [if one struck] upon its tail and it went toward its head, [the staff] struck upon its neck. And we do not read "and even"; for [the Gemara] says "along the entire spine" specifically [when] one did not bend the staff and struck across all the ribs:

Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:3.hebrew: ואי שלים חוטרא אפלגא דגבא - שלא היה ארוך ככל השדרה, חיישינן:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:3.english: And if the stick ended at the middle of the back - Since it was not as long as the entire spine, we are concerned.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:4.english: Knots - In [the case of] a stick that has remnants of branches.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:5.hebrew: אפסקיה - בהפסק, כלומר: לרוחב הגב — חיישינן לחוט השדרה:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:12:5.english: Crosswise - Transversely, that is to say, across the width of the back — we are concerned for [injury to] the spinal cord.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:13:1.hebrew: בית הרחם - עגל שנולד היום, שיצא מבית הרחם צר:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:13:1.english: The womb - A calf that was born today, which emerged from a narrow womb.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:13:2.hebrew: אין חוששין - שמא נדחק ונתרסקו אבריו, ואין צריך להשהותו מעת לעת:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:13:2.english: One does not suspect - That it was compressed and its limbs crushed, and there is no need to delay it for a twenty-four-hour period.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:1:1.english: It is certain that [it occurred] before slaughter - And [it is] a tereifah.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:2:2.hebrew: בידוע שהוא ג' ימים קודם שחיטה - ואם לקחה בתוך שלשה ימים, הוי מקח טעות, וצריך המוכר להחזיר לו מעותיו:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:2:2.english: It is certain that it was three days before slaughter - And if he bought it within three days, it is a mistaken transaction, and the seller must return his money to him.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:2:3.hebrew: לא הוגלד פי המכה - איכא לספוקי אי קודם מקח הוי, אי לאחר מקח הוי. ועל הטבח — שהוא מוציא מידו, דמסתמא כל כמה דלא יהיב זוזי לא יהבי ליה חיותא — ועליו להביא ראיה שקודם מקח הוה, דמספיקא לא מפקינן ממונא מחזקיה. למאי נפקא מינה — לא גרסינן:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:2:3.english: The opening of the wound did not scab over - There is uncertainty whether it occurred before the purchase or whether it occurred after the purchase. And [the burden of proof rests] upon the butcher, who is seeking to extract [money] from his [the seller's] possession — for presumably, as long as he had not given the money, they would not have given him the animal — and [so] upon him [rests the burden] to bring proof that it occurred before the purchase, for out of doubt we do not extract money from its possessor. [The words] “To what practical difference” — we do not read in the text.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:3:1.hebrew: התם ליכא מידי למיסרך - כשנמצא נקב בלא מחט — כשהדם יוצא, הוא מתקנח בלחלוחית הבשר והולך, לפי שאין לו היכן לידבק:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:3:1.english: There, there is nothing for [it] to adhere to - When a perforation is found without a needle: when the blood emerges, it is wiped away by the moisture of the flesh and disappears, since it has nowhere to adhere.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:3:2.english: It would have attached - The blood to the needle.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:4:1.english: Rav Avira appointed me - [The text should read:] “Rav Avira is my name.”

Rashi on Chullin 51a:4:2.english: He sent to him - Abaye [sent to him], that he should come to him.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:1.hebrew: מפטיר כנסיות אנא - מכניס ומוציא תלמידים, ומאספם, ומעמידם לילך מבית המדרש:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:1.english: I am a director of assemblies - [One who] ushers students in and out, gathering them and having them rise to leave the study hall.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:2.hebrew: לעילא מרבי רבה - מר' יהודה הנשיא:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:2.english: Above the Great Rabbi - [Above] Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:3.hebrew: רב הונא צפוראה ור' יוסי מדאה:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:3.english: Rav Huna of Tzippori and Rabbi Yosei of Media:

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:4.english: A needle that was found in the thickness of the reticulum - From the inside.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:5.english: From one side - That it was not visible from the outside.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:6.english: And he turned it over - [He turned] the reticulum to the outer side.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:7.hebrew: ומצא - על המחט, כנגד פיה מבחוץ, קורט דם:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:7.english: And he found - On the needle, opposite its point on the outside, a drop of blood.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:8.hebrew: אמר אם אין מכה - זו יוצאת לחוץ, דם זה מנין כאן:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:8.english: He said: If there is no wound - [meaning, if] this [wound does not] emerge to the outside, from where is this blood here?

Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:9.hebrew: טרח טריח לההוא גברא - "כמה הטרחת לאותו האיש!" על עצמו היה אומר, שהטריחו זה לבא אצלו. לישנא אחרינא: טרח טרייה — כמו "דטרייה לרישיה" דאמרן לעיל (חולין דף מה:); כלומר, בחנם טרחתי לבא, שאין כאן דבר חדוש:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:5:9.english: Trouble has troubled that man - “How much you have troubled that man!” — He was saying [this] about himself, for this [person] had troubled him to come to him. Another version: Tarach taryei — like “detaryei lereishei” [who banged his head], which we said above (Chullin 45b); that is to say: In vain did I trouble myself to come, for there is nothing novel here.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:6:3.hebrew: אין חוששין - הואיל ולא ראינוה שנפלה, אין חוששין שמא נתרסקו אבריה להשהותה מעת לעת כדין נפולה ורסוקת אברים, דאמרינן במתניתין (לקמן חולין נו.) גבי עוף: אם שהתה מעת לעת ושחטה — כשרה; ובקופצת מאליה, לא חיישינן להכי:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:6:3.english: One need not be concerned - Since we did not see it fall, one need not be concerned that perhaps its limbs were shattered, [so as to require] delaying [its slaughter] for twenty-four hours in accordance with the law of a fallen [animal] and [one with] shattered limbs, as we say in our Mishnah (below, Chullin 56a) regarding a bird: If it lingered for twenty-four hours and he slaughtered it, it is kosher; and in [the case of an animal that] jumps of its own accord, we are not concerned about this.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:1.hebrew: ההוא גדיא דהוה ליה לרבינא - בגג, והוה ארובה בגג:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:1.english: A certain kid belonging to Ravina - [It was] on the roof, and there was a skylight in the roof.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:3.hebrew: באיפומא - כנגד פי ארובה, למטה בבית:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:3.english: At the opening - Opposite the opening of the skylight, below in the house.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:5.hebrew: משום דאית לה מידי למסרך - שלא קפצה דרך ארובה, אלא בצידי הגג — מסרכת עצמה בכתלים וקופצת, ומהניא לה סריכת הכתלים שמסרכת בידיה קצת:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:5.english: Because it has something to grab hold of - That it did not jump through a skylight, but rather at the sides of the roof: it clings to the walls and jumps, and the clinging to the walls — in that it clings a bit with its forelegs — is effective for it.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:6.english: And this [kid] has nothing to grab hold of - For the skylight was not adjacent to the wall.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:7.hebrew: דאמדה נפשה - אם גבוה לה יותר מדאי, אינה קופצת:
Rashi on Chullin 51a:7:7.english: That it evaluates itself - If it is too high for it, it does not jump.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:9:1.english: Whose hind legs were dragging - Its hind legs were dragging behind it.

Rashi on Chullin 51a:9:3.english: The halakha is in accordance with Rav Yeimar - That we do not need to inspect other animals whose legs drag.

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:10:1.hebrew: נפל לארעא חוששין - אף על גב דבנפילה בעינן עד שיפול מעשרה טפחים, כדאיתא בפרק שור שנגח את הפרה (ב"ק דף נ:), ומכריסא דתורא עד ארעא ליכא אלא ארבעה טפחים, כדאמר התם (דף נא.) — מ"מ חיישינן הכא, משום דנפיל מחמת ההכאה שמנגחין זה את זה:
Tosafot on Chullin 51a:10:1.english: [If it] fell to the ground, we are concerned - Even though with regard to a fall we require that it fall from [a height of] ten handbreadths, as stated in the chapter [entitled] Shor SheNagach Et HaParah (Bava Kamma 50b), and from the belly of an ox to the ground there are only four handbreadths, as [the Gemara] says there (51a) — nevertheless, we are concerned here, because it fell due to the blow of their butting one another.

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:13:1.hebrew: בית הרחם אין בו משום ריסוק אברים - משום דאיכא ריעותא דאינו הולך, איצטריך ליה לאשמועינן; דאי לאו הכי, פשיטא דאזלינן בתר רוב ולדות. וא"ת: א"כ, מאי קא מסייע ליה מבן יום אחד דמטמא בזיבה? התם ליכא ריעותא, א"נ כשחיה הרבה אחרי כן! וי"ל: דאם איתא דאתרמי ריסוק אברים מחמת בית הרחם, א"כ היה לנו לחושבו לאונס לענין זיבה. ועוד, דזובו מוכיח שנתרסקו אבריו בבית הרחם, וכעין ריעותא הוא, דמסתמא דמחמת כך בא הזוב; אלא ודאי, לעולם אין בו ריסוק אברים:
Tosafot on Chullin 51a:13:1.english: The womb is not subject to [concern about] shattered limbs - Because there is an apparent defect in that it does not walk, he needed to teach us [this]; for were it not so, it would be obvious, as we follow the majority of newborns. And if you say: If so, why does [Rava] bring support for him from a one-day-old infant who becomes ritually impure through zivah? There, there is no apparent defect; alternatively, [the baraita speaks of a case] where he lived a long time thereafter! And one can say: That if it were so that shattered limbs occur due to the womb, if so, we should have considered it an accident with regard to zivah. And furthermore, his discharge proves that his limbs were shattered in the womb, and it is akin to an apparent defect, as presumably the discharge came about because of that. Rather, certainly, [the womb] never causes shattered limbs.

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:2:1.hebrew: המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה - פירוש: על הלוקח להביא ראיה שברשות מוכר נטרפה. אע"פ שלא נתן מעות עדיין — כאן נמצאו וכאן היו, כדאמר בסוף פרק המדיר (כתובות דף עו:). והא דקרי ליה מוציא — משום דמסתמא כל כמה דלא יהיב זוזי, לא יהיב ליה חיותא. והקשה ה"ר י"ט, דבנדה פרק הרואה כתם (נדה דף נח.) תניא: בדקה עצמה וחלוקה והשאילתה לחברתה — היא טהורה וחברתה תולה; ומפרש רב ששת דלענין דינא תנן, דלא מיחייבא חברתה לכבס הבגד. ואמאי לא אמרינן כאן נמצאו וכאן היו, כמו גבי בהמה דהכא וגבי מומין דסוף המדיר? וי"ל: דלא דמי; דודאי כדי לקיים המכר ובקדושין, סברא הוא דאמרינן הכי, שאומר המוכר ללוקח: "קח פרתך, שברשותך נטרפה", והאב אומר לבעל: "קח אשתך, שברשותך נולד המום", ואין לנו לבטל המעשה הזה; אבל גבי חלוק — ליכא למימר הכי. ועוד, גבי חלוק — לעולם הוא ברשות הראשונה, בעלת חלוק, שלא בא ליד השניה בתורת מכר אלא בתורת שאילה, ולא שייך למימר ברשות שואלה נמצאת ולא ברשות בעלת חלוק:
Tosafot on Chullin 51a:2:1.english: The burden of proof rests upon the claimant - The explanation is that it is upon the buyer to bring proof that it became a tereifah in the seller's domain. Even if he has not yet paid money, [we say,] "Here they were found, and here they were [presumed to have been]," as [the Gemara] says at the end of the chapter [entitled] Hamadir (Ketubot 76b). And that which [the baraita] calls him a "claimant" [motzi, literally "one who extracts"] is because ordinarily, as long as [a buyer] does not give money, [the seller] does not give him the animal. And Rabbi Yom Tov raised a difficulty: For in Niddah, in the chapter [entitled] Haroeh Kettem (Niddah 58a), it is taught [in a baraita]: If [a woman] examined herself and her robe, and lent it to another woman, she is pure and her friend may attribute [any bloodstain found on the robe to the first woman]. And Rav Sheshet explains that we learned [this] with regard to a monetary judgment, that her friend is not obligated to launder the garment. But why do we not say, "Here they were found, and here they were," as [we do] regarding the animal here and regarding blemishes at the end of [the chapter entitled] Hamadir? And one can say that they are not comparable: For certainly, in order to uphold the sale, and in [the case of] betrothal, it is logical that we say this, as the seller says to the buyer: "Take your cow, for it became a tereifah in your possession," and the father says to the husband: "Take your wife, for the blemish arose in your possession," and we should not void this transaction; but regarding a robe, one cannot say this. And furthermore, regarding the robe, it is always in the domain of the first [woman], the owner of the robe, because it did not enter the hands of the second [woman] by way of sale, but rather by way of a loan, and it is not applicable to say that it was found in the borrower's domain and not in the robe owner's domain.

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:3:1.hebrew: כיון דאיכא מחט מסרך הוה סריך - ה"ה קוץ וכל דבר. תדע, מדקאמר: "התם ליכא מידי למיסרך":
Tosafot on Chullin 51a:3:1.english: "Since there is a needle, [the blood] would have attached" - The same applies to a thorn or any [such] object. Know [this], from the fact that [the Gemara] says: "There, there is nothing to [which the blood can] attach."

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:7:1.hebrew: דגר ונפל - ולא הלך, דלקמן פסקינן דהלכה — אפילו בדיקה לא בעי:
Tosafot on Chullin 51a:7:1.english: "It jumped and fell" - And it did not walk [afterward], for later on we rule that [if] it walked, it does not even require an inspection.

Tosafot on Chullin 51a:9:1.english: "Whose hind legs would drag" - It is not dealing with a fall.
